results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: The availability you send (in stock, out of stock, preorder or backorder) must match what the product page and checkout show. If they differ, Google disapproves the product.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: This often happens because of a delay between changing stock on your website and updating your product data.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: A GTIN is the barcode number a manufacturer gives a product, such as a UPC in North America or an EAN in Europe. Google recommends sending it for every product that has one.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Products with a missing or wrong GTIN may get limited visibility. If a product does have a GTIN and you leave it out, the product could be disapproved.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Valid GTINs are 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits long. Spaces and dashes are ignored. The last digit is a check digit and must be correct, so copy the number exactly from the packaging or from your supplier.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Only send a GTIN you are sure is right, and never make one up. Numbers starting with 02, 04 or 2 are restricted, and numbers starting with 05, 98 or 99 are coupon numbers, so neither kind is accepted.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: If a product really has no GTIN, such as a store brand or private label item, do not send one. Send the brand and the manufacturer part number (MPN) instead.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: The identifier exists setting tells Google that a product has no unique product identifiers at all: no GTIN, no MPN and no brand.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: Set it to "no" only for products that truly have none, such as custom made goods, handmade or one of a kind items, and vintage or antique items.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: Only use "no" when you are certain. If Google finds evidence that the product does have identifiers, the product gets a warning.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: The price you send must match the price shown on the product's page and at checkout, in the same currency. If they differ, Google disapproves the product.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: Common causes are a delay between changing the price on your website and updating your product data, a sale price with the wrong dates, or price markup on the page that differs from the price shoppers see.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To fix it, change the price in your product data so it matches the product page exactly, then upload the corrected data. You can edit products one at a time in Merchant Center or download the list of affected products and fix them in bulk.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: After the fix, Google's crawler rechecks disapproved products over the next few hours or days. Once the prices match, the product is approved again.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To stop it happening again, update your product data on a regular schedule so prices change in both places at the same time.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Merchant Center can update some product information automatically, using what it finds on your website. Automatic item updates cover price, sale price, availability and condition.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: It works by reading the structured data (schema.org markup) on your product pages, and other information on the page. If your product data says one thing and the website says another, for example $4 in your data but $3 on the page, the product is updated to match the website. This helps avoid some price and availability mismatches.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Automatic item updates are on by default. You can turn them on or off under Products, on the Automations tab, by choosing an automation and opening View details.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Automatic updates are not a replacement for keeping your product data up to date. They are meant for occasional mismatches on a small share of products. If a price or availability changes often, for example more than once a day, the product may be disapproved instead of updated.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Updates may also not work if your product pages have no structured data, or the markup is incomplete or incorrect. If a page shows several strikethrough prices, the right one may not be found. For sale prices, check that the sale price effective date and its time zone are correct. Updates can also stop if the number of mismatches becomes too large.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: Product issues only affect the products involved. Account issues affect every product in the account. Product issues are listed on the Needs attention tab under Products, and account issues show in a banner at the top of Merchant Center.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: To fix a product issue, correct the product data and upload it again. Some issues also offer a suggested automatic fix in Merchant Center.

results.title: What happens after you fix a product
results.passage: After you update your products, Google checks them again. These checks usually finish within 24 to 48 hours, and products show as pending while they are reviewed.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: Every product needs a main image link. Without one the product cannot show.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: The link must be a full web address that starts with http:// or https://.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: The image must show the actual product. Placeholder images, generic images and graphics that do not show the product are not allowed.

results.title: Product image link
results.passage: Images must be at least 500 by 500 pixels, and around 1500 by 1500 pixels or larger is recommended. Do not add promotional text, logos, watermarks or other overlays to the main image.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: Merchant Center can try to fix product images that were disapproved because of promotional overlays. It removes text, watermarks, overlays or logos it detects in the image.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: Automatic image improvements are off by default. You can turn them on under Products, on the Automations tab.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: They may not fix every image. Merchant Center does not try when the result would be poor, for example complex multi-panel collages, heavy text over the main product, or strong or dense watermarks. In those cases, upload an image that follows the image requirements.

results.title: Automatic image improvements
results.passage: Image improvements work on the overlays in an existing image. A missing image or a placeholder needs a real image of the product, added by you.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: Every product needs a title, and it can be at most 150 characters long.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: A good title says clearly what the product is, using specific words. Include the brand and key details such as size, color and material, especially when they tell variants apart.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: Do not put prices, shipping details or promotional text in the title. Avoid all capital letters, symbols, HTML and extra spaces.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: To fix a title that is too long, shorten it to 150 characters or less and keep the most important details near the start.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: The availability you send (in stock, out of stock, preorder or backorder) must match what the product page and checkout show. If they differ, Google disapproves the product.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: This often happens because of a delay between changing stock on your website and updating your product data.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: To fix it, change the availability in your product data to match the product page, then upload the corrected data. You can edit products one at a time in Merchant Center or download the list of affected products and fix them in bulk.

results.title: Availability in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: After the fix, it can take some time before the product's status updates. Google may take up to 12 hours to review your website, and once the values match the product shows again.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: In the United States and many other countries, products need shipping information, including cost and delivery speed. Products with missing or wrong shipping information can be disapproved.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: The recommended way is to set up shipping in your Merchant Center account settings, which then applies to your products. Use the shipping value in your product data only to override those settings for specific products.

results.title: Shipping costs
results.passage: Delivery speed is made of two parts: handling time, from the order until it is handed to the carrier, and transit time, from the carrier to the customer.

results.title: CBD and other unapproved substances
results.passage: Google's list of unapproved pharmaceuticals and supplements includes cannabidiol (CBD). Products on this list are not allowed in Shopping ads or free listings.

results.title: CBD and other unapproved substances
results.passage: This is a policy decision, not a data problem, so it cannot be fixed by editing product details. Whether a specific product is allowed is decided by Google's policy team under the healthcare and medicines policy.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: When a product or account has an issue, Merchant Center may offer a "Request review" option. For product issues it is in the product's details on the Needs attention tab. For account issues it is under View setup and policy issues.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: There are two choices: "I fixed the issue", if you have made the change, or "I disagree with the issue", if you think Google's decision is wrong. If you disagree, you may need to give a reason or upload documents, and you may be asked to verify your identity.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: You may only get one chance to disagree before a waiting period starts, so it is worth getting the request right.

results.title: Requesting a review or appealing a decision
results.passage: A review can take up to 7 business days. Your ads may not show while the account or products are under review.
